title: Deprecation orchestration and backward-compatibility probes for streaming/tool-calls/structured-output
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Goal: implement an orchestration layer, rollout plan, and automated probe suite to safely deprecate legacy behavior flags and validate backward compatibility across streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output features. Scope includes: 1) a controlled flag-deprecation workflow (staged opt-out windows, canary cohorts, auto rollback), 2) an extensible test harness that runs deterministic end-to-end probes against streaming+tool-call scenarios and structured-output schemas, and 3) migration guide artifacts for SDKs and Console. The system must detect semantic regressions (format/schema changes, missing function call events, stream truncation) and trigger automatic mitigation (rollback or switch to compatibility shim).
acceptance_criteria: Orchestration API supports: schedule_deprecation(flag, start_date, cohorts) and immediate_abort(deprecation_id)
Probe harness runs nightly against prod-like staging with >95% scenario coverage for streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs
Automated comparison detects: missing tool invocation logs, structured-output schema drift, and streaming delta (token-level divergence)
Rollback policy triggers within 5 minutes on high-severity regression and creates an incident with runbook link
Migration guide draft and SDK snippets published to Confluence and linked in Console feature deprecation banner
plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): design orchestration API, define canary cohorts, and draft migration guide. Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement probe harness with synthetic workloads and schema assertions. Phase 3 (2 weeks): integrate with rollout engine, add automated rollback, and run a full suite against Dedicated + Private stacks. Phase 4 (1 week): docs, SDK patches, and Console banner + telemetry. Parallel: security review and compliance checks.
notes: We must avoid wide opt-outs that leave traffic untested. Prior incidents (INC-2025-11) showed silent regressions when streaming framing changed; lessons learned are folded into probe scenarios. Quant metrics to track: percent of requests covered by probes, mean time-to-detect (MTTD), mean time-to-rollback (MTTR), and false-positive rate for schema drift detectors.
updates: 2026-02-11 — Kickoff: aligned on scope with PM and DX; agreed to prioritize streaming and function-call probes first.
2026-02-15 — Prototype: implemented probe runner skeleton that can replay recorded sessions and validate tool-call events (PR opened, awaiting review).
2026-02-22 — Review feedback from Security: must sign all probe payloads with ephemeral KMS key when running against staging clusters (ticket queued to infra).
2026-02-28 — Added structured-output schema comparator using json-schema + fuzzy-key matcher to handle optional fields; initial false-positive tuning ongoing.
2026-03-05 — Canary plan approved by SRE; cohorts defined by tenant size and SLA tier. Added metric dashboards (probe pass rate, drift score).

2026-03-10 — Integration test failure: streaming probe occasionally sees truncated final event when using low-latency batching config on Dedicated. Incident logged; mitigations: tighten batch flush timeout and add an extra stream-sentinel marker in probes.
risks: False positives from schema comparator could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; requires careful thresholding and human-in-the-loop confirmation for P2 regressions.
Running probes at scale may incur noticeable cost; need quota controls and sampling strategies for night runs.
Compatibility shims add code-path complexity and long-term maintenance burden — schedule tech-debt paydown after deprecation complete.
